text:
nora: reprod a pretty reliable hang in the go generator example when cancelling during the token refresh handshake window. gist with harness: https://internal.gists/redwood/stream-hang-3765
ishaan: can you paste the minimal stack? sounds like the auth refresher/thread isn't observing ctx.Done()
paul: these usually show as goroutines stuck in a channel send/recv between refresher and reader. go prefers explicit Close() semantics so ambiguous ownership bites us here.
nora: stack excerpt: `goroutine 67 [chan receive]:\n  github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go/stream.(*reader).run(0xc000...)\n  /repo/sdk-go/stream/reader.go:78 +0x...` and `goroutine 68 [chan send]:\n  github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go/auth.(*refresher).notify(0xc000...)\n  /repo/sdk-go/auth/refresher.go:44 +0x...`
tara: probable cause: refresher does `authCh <- token` without selecting on ctx.Done(), so if the reader returned and nobody receives, refresher blocks forever. simple fix: select with ctx.Done() when notifying.
ishaan: agreed. but bigger picture: our current public API `Subscribe()` returns a channel and spawns runtime goroutines. cancellation semantics are fuzzy: who closes what? we should consider a small ergonomics change: a pull-style Stream API `Pull(ctx, req) (Stream, error)` where `Stream.Recv(ctx)` and `Stream.Close()` are explicit. that makes cancellation explicit and idiomatic for Go.
paul: `Recv(ctx)` matches io/reader-like patterns and makes it obvious callers must pass ctx to every blocking read. we can keep `Subscribe()` as a shim that adapts the new Stream back to channel semantics for compatibility.
tara: tests: add `TestCancelDuringHandshake_noGoroutineLeak` under `stream/stream_test.go` and use a harness to count goroutines before/after. I can add a tiny example in `sdk/go/examples/generator-cancel` that shows the pattern `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(...); defer cancel(); stream, _ := client.Pull(ctx, req); defer stream.Close(); for { chunk, err := stream.Recv(ctx); if err != nil { break } }`.
nora: I implemented the select-on-ctx for the refresher and added the Recv/Close prototype in a branch. Running the harness shows master leaks ~3 goroutines per cancel, patched branch shows zero leaks. CI link: https://ci.internal/streams/3765
ishaan: parity note: python and ts SDKs currently close net.Conn on cancel which unwinds all goroutines. Go should prefer explicit Recv(ctx)+Close() semantics but we must document the behavioral difference. add a short section in `docs/sdk/go/streaming.md` and a migration note.
paul: also add a small compatibility shim so existing users calling `Subscribe()` don't break: the shim returns a channel and launches a goroutine that reads from Stream.Recv(ctx) and forwards chunks to the channel, ensuring Close() is called when ctx cancels. emit a deprecation warning in logs.
tara: performance: Recv(ctx) adds a ctx check but overhead is negligible vs network. still add a benchmark `BenchmarkStreamRecv` in `stream/bench_test.go`. I'll run perf matrix across small/large payloads.
ci-bot: created issue #5233 "go sdk: generator stream hang during token refresh" and attached test failure for `TestCancelDuringHandshake`.
nora: I'll open an RFC (rfc/000-streaming-v2.md) proposing the v2 pull-style API, include migration guide, example apps, tests, and a minimal shim. tagging @ishaan @paul @tara for review.
ishaan: please include a short changelog entry and a Dedicated migration note since some infra teams embed the go client tightly.
paul: UX nit: examples should use `defer stream.Close()` in the top of the function so newbies don't forget. also show context timeout pattern.
tara: once RFC lands I'll help with benchmarks and docs. great catch nora :rocket:
